title: Grhastha — Guided Puja at Home
summary: A calm, guided way for Hindu households to perform authentic puja at home — accurate timing, step-by-step guidance, and the mantras with their meaning — designed to preserve authenticity and access rather than gamify devotion.
problem: Doing a puja properly at home means knowing three hard things at once: when it should happen, how to actually perform it, and what the words mean. That knowledge is often scattered, inconsistent online, or lost between generations — and most apps in the space lean on subscriptions, logins, and merchandising that sit awkwardly with something sacred.
approach: Shaped the product around three pillars — Know When, Know How, Know the Words — and a firm set of principles: no login, no subscription, calm and devotional rather than SaaS-looking, authentic rather than gamified, with a sacred-calendar / almanac feeling and a Madhubani-inspired Ganesh visual language. First-run onboarding only; on later visits you go straight to the home experience. Initial focus is Ganesh Chaturthi, with other festivals to follow.
outcome: A product designed to reduce complexity without reducing authenticity: households get accurate, location-aware timing, unhurried step-by-step guidance, and the mantras in Sanskrit with transliteration, audio, and meaning — no account, no paywall.
